s170-m04: the s169 hygiene basket is closed, 6/6, and two of the items produced evidence worth keeping. (1) THE FF#22 FIXTURE'S DEGENERACY WAS PROVEN RATHER THAN ASSUMED (#1126). I reconstructed the pre-s170 fixture and ran it against a first-entry-only mutant of applyLayerOrdering: it passed 5/5, so it genuinely could not tell the shipped implementation from a much weaker one. The cause is worth generalising: the old fixture ordered ['target','baseline','actual'] over the declaration [baseline,actual,target], and for THAT pairing a first-entry-only implementation emits the identical result — the test was blind not because it was weak in form but because its DATA happened to be a fixed point of the weaker implementation. Choosing ['actual','target','baseline'] breaks the coincidence (full ordering gives ['actual','target','baseline'], first-entry-only gives ['actual','baseline','target']), and the divergence is now asserted explicitly with .not.toEqual so the discrimination is a property of the test rather than a fact someone has to notice. Under the mutant the new fixture reds 2 and all three keep-greens stay green. LESSON: an ordering test must pick a permutation that is NOT a fixed point of the degenerate implementation, and should assert the degenerate output is not produced. (2) The scratchpad untrack kept NINETEEN files rather than the three the critic found, because the charter says 'test/doc' and committed MEMOS cite 16 more by path — including a brace-expanded citation, scratchpad/s169-m02/{head-mutated,rewired,rewired-mutated}.test.ts, that a naive path grep would have missed entirely. Both directions were verified (every kept file not ignored, every dropped file ignored, zero dangling citations). Three cited paths were ALREADY absent from disk beforehand (s154/s161 memos citing scratchpad/f2-synth-verify.ts and scratchpad/m2_final_predicate.mjs) — pre-existing dangling references, recorded so they are not mistaken for damage from this change.
